1.q: Priya draws 3 triangles and 2 squares. How many corners do all her shapes have altogether?
1.hint: A triangle has 3 corners and a square has 4 corners. Count the corners of each kind of shape.
1.why: 3 × 3 = 9 and 2 × 4 = 8. Add them: 9 + 8 = 17 corners.

1.q: Ali, Ben and Chen stand in a line to buy a drink. How many different orders can the three friends stand in?
1.hint: Choose who is first. Then see who can be second.
1.why: Any of 3 friends can be first. Then 2 friends are left for second, and 1 for last. 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders.

1.q: In a number pyramid, each brick is the sum of the two bricks under it. The bottom row is 3, 8, 9. What number is on the top brick?
1.hint: Find the middle row first. Then add the two bricks in the middle row.
1.why: The middle row is 11 and 17. The top brick is the sum of the middle row: 28.

1.q: Kumar doubled the number of marbles he had. Now he has 18 marbles. How many marbles did he have before?
1.hint: Doubling is adding the number to itself. What number added to itself makes 18?
1.why: A number plus itself is 18. 9 + 9 = 18, so Kumar had 9 marbles.

1.q: One digit in this sum is hidden: 4_ + 17 = 62. Which digit goes in the blank?
1.hint: The ones digits: 7 plus what digit gives a number that ends in 2? Then check the tens.
1.why: Check 45 + 17 = 62. The hidden digit is 5.

1.q: In a class of 20 children, 12 like apples and 10 like bananas. Every child likes at least one of the two fruits. How many children like both fruits?
1.hint: Add the apple lovers and the banana lovers. Is the answer more than the class?
1.why: 12 + 10 = 22, but the class has only 20 children. The extra 2 were counted twice, so 2 children like both.

1.q: Daniel has 15 stickers. Nurul has 6 more than Daniel. Arjun has 4 more than Nurul. How many stickers does Arjun have?
1.hint: Find Nurul's stickers first.
1.why: Nurul has 21. Arjun has 21 + 4 = 25 stickers.

1.q: A card is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. A beetle crawls along all four edges of the card. How far does the beetle crawl?
1.hint: A card has two long sides and two short sides.

1.q: Wei Jie lists every number from 1 to 35 that is in the 5 times table. How many numbers are on his list?
1.hint: The 5 times table goes 5, 10, 15 ... Keep going and stop before you pass 35.
1.why: The numbers are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35. That is 7 numbers.

1.q: How many different pairs of whole numbers (not 0) add up to 12? Count 1 + 11 and 11 + 1 as one pair.
1.hint: Start with 1 and its partner. Then try 2 and its partner. Stop when the pairs start to repeat.
1.why: The pairs are 1 + 11, 2 + 10, 3 + 9, 4 + 8, 5 + 7, 6 + 6. After 6 + 6 the pairs only repeat in the other order, so there are 6 pairs.

1.q: One box holds 3 bags. Each bag holds 4 sweets. Aisha buys 3 boxes. How many sweets does she have?
1.hint: Find how many sweets are in one box first.
1.why: One box has 3 bags of 4 sweets, which is 12 sweets. 3 boxes have 12 + 12 + 12 = 36 sweets.

1.q: How many whole numbers are there between 30 and 54? Do not count 30 or 54.
1.hint: Write the first whole number after 30 and the last one before 54. Then count them.
1.why: The numbers are from 31 to 53. Counting them gives 23 numbers.

1.q: Hui Min opens her purse and finds 3 ten-cent coins and 4 five-cent coins. How many cents is that in all?
1.hint: Count the ten-cent coins in tens. Then count the five-cent coins in fives.

1.q: Priya had some stickers. Her aunt gave her 7 more stickers. Now she has 15 stickers. How many stickers did Priya have at first?
1.hint: Work backwards. Take away the stickers her aunt gave her.
1.why: Priya has 15 now. Take away the 7 stickers from her aunt: 15 − 7 = 8 stickers.

1.q: Kumar ties sticks into bundles of 10. He has 3 bundles and 14 single sticks. What is the total number of sticks?
1.hint: Count the bundles in tens first. Then add the single sticks.
1.why: 3 bundles is 30 sticks. 30 + 14 = 44 sticks.

1.q: Find the missing number: 7 + 8 = 9 + ?
1.hint: Work out the left side first. The right side must be the same.
1.why: 7 + 8 = 15. The right side must also make 15, so 9 + 6 = 15.

1.q: Hui Min has three number cards: 5, 2 and 9. She picks two cards to make the biggest 2-digit number she can. What is it?
1.hint: The biggest card should go in the tens place.
1.why: Put the biggest card, 9, in the tens place. Then put the next biggest, 5, in the ones place. The number is 95.

1.q: A table shows how many pupils walked to school: Monday 12, Tuesday 9, Wednesday 15, Thursday 11. How many pupils walked on these four days altogether?
1.hint: Add two days at a time. You can add the tens first and then the ones.

1.q: Pick any three odd numbers, like 3, 5 and 7, and add them up. Is the sum odd or even?
1.hint: Try adding some triples from 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9. Look at the totals.
1.why: Two odd numbers make an even number. An even number plus one more odd number is odd. So the answer is odd.

1.q: Farhan has number cards 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9. How many different pairs of cards add up to 11?
1.hint: Take the 2 card first. Which card goes with it? Then try the next card.
1.why: The pairs are 2 + 9 and 5 + 6. Each pair adds up to 11, so there are 2 pairs.

1.q: Mei Ling faces north. She turns right, then turns right again, then turns left. Which way does she face now: north, east, south or west?
1.hint: Draw a small compass. Turn one step at a time and write the direction after each turn.
1.why: Facing north, then east, then south, then east. After the three turns Mei Ling faces east.

1.q: A big square is split into 4 small squares, 2 rows of 2. Counting squares of every size, how many are there in the drawing?
1.hint: Start with the smallest squares. Then look for a larger square made from several of them.
1.why: There are 4 small squares and 1 big square made of all four. 4 + 1 = 5 squares.

1.q: Priya has 43 stickers and Ben has 16 stickers. How many more stickers does Priya have than Ben?
1.hint: Line the stickers up in two rows. Count the ones that have no partner.
1.why: Take away the smaller number from the bigger number: 43 − 16 = 27 stickers.

1.q: Mei Ling sorts these numbers: 14, 22, 9, 31, 28, 40, 17 and 26. She keeps only the numbers that are even and bigger than 20. How many numbers does she keep?
1.hint: Check each number twice: is it even, and is it bigger than 20?
1.why: The numbers that pass both checks are 22, 28, 40, 26. That is 4 numbers.

1.q: Hui Min writes the numbers from 1 to 30. How many of her numbers have the digit 2 in them? (2, 12 and 25 are some of them.)
1.hint: Write them in groups: 1 to 9, 10 to 19, 20 to 29, and 30.
1.why: The numbers are 2, 12, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28 and 29. That is 12 numbers.

1.q: In 47, how much more is the value of the digit 4 than the digit 7?
1.hint: The 4 is in the tens place. The 7 is in the ones place. Write the value of each.
1.why: The 4 means 40. The 7 means 7. 40 − 7 = 33.

1.q: Priya wants to pay exactly 35 cents. She has many coins of each kind: 5 cents, 10 cents, 20 cents and 50 cents. What is the fewest coins she needs?
1.hint: Use the biggest coin that fits first. Then see what is left to pay.
1.why: Use a 20-cent coin, then a 10-cent coin, then a 5-cent coin: 20 + 10 + 5. Together that is 3 coins.

1.q: Beads are strung in this order again and again: pink, blue, blue. The string has 12 beads. How many of them are blue?
1.hint: Write the order out in groups of 3 until you have all the beads.
1.why: The pattern is 3 beads long and the string has 4 whole patterns. Each pattern has 2 blue beads. 2 × 4 = 8 beads.

1.q: Kumar lays a pencil beside a ruler. Its left end is at the 4 cm mark and its right end is at the 13 cm mark. How long is the pencil?
1.hint: Do not read the number at the right end only. Count the cm steps between the two ends.
1.why: Count the cm from 4 to 13. The pencil is 9 cm long.

1.q: Uncle has 20 oranges. Each bag holds 5 oranges. How many bags will he fill?
1.hint: Count in 5s until you reach 20.
1.why: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 counts of 5, so Uncle fills 4 bags.

1.q: Ali, Siti and Ravi each own one pet: a cat, a fish or a bird. Ali owns neither the cat nor the fish. Siti does not own the cat. Which friend owns the fish?
1.hint: Start with the friend who has only one pet left to choose from.
1.why: Ali does not have the cat or the fish, so Ali has the bird. Siti does not have the cat and the bird is taken, so Siti has the fish. Ravi has the cat. So Siti has the fish.

2.q: A library lends 245 books on Monday, 318 on Tuesday and 126 on Wednesday. How many books does it lend on these three days altogether?
2.hint: Add the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones. Or add two days first.

2.q: The school concert lasts 2 hours and 15 minutes. How many minutes is that?
2.hint: One hour is 60 minutes. Change the hours to minutes first.
2.why: 2 hours is 120 minutes. 120 + 15 = 135 minutes.

2.q: Aisha, Ben, Chen and Dina each order one drink: milk tea, juice, water or soya milk. Aisha orders neither juice nor water. Ben does not order milk tea. Chen orders water. Dina orders neither juice nor soya milk. Who orders the juice?
2.hint: Chen has water. Put that drink aside and see who is left for each other drink.
2.why: Aisha orders the soya milk, Ben orders the juice, Chen orders the water, Dina orders the milk tea. So Ben orders the juice.

2.q: Daniel has 125 stickers. Nurul has 40 fewer than Daniel. Arjun has 55 more than Nurul. How many stickers does Arjun have?
2.hint: Find Nurul's stickers first.
2.why: Nurul has 125 − 40 = 85. Arjun has 85 + 55 = 140 stickers.

2.q: Ali, Ben, Chen and Dina line up to buy tickets. How many different orders can the four friends stand in?
2.hint: Choose who is first. Then think about who can be second, and so on.
2.why: 4 choices for first, then 3, then 2, then 1. 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 orders.

2.q: Uncle's rope is 2 m 65 cm long. How many centimetres is that?
2.hint: 1 m is 100 cm. Change the metres to centimetres first.

2.q: Look at the numbers from 10 to 60. In how many of them is the ones digit smaller than the tens digit? (31 is one, because 1 is smaller than 3.)
2.hint: Go through the tens one at a time: 10 to 19, 20 to 29, and so on.
2.why: Count by tens. The 10s have 1 (10), the 20s have 2, the 30s have 3, the 40s have 4, the 50s have 5, and 60 is one more: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 1 = 16 numbers.

2.q: A robot starts at the top-left corner of a grid. It moves only 3 steps right and 2 steps down, in any order, to reach the bottom-right corner. How many different routes can it take?
2.hint: Count the routes to each corner of the grid, starting next to the start.
2.why: Add the routes from the left and from above at every corner. The bottom-right corner gets 10 routes.

2.q: A school trip has 46 children, and every van seats 8 of them. How many vans must the school book so that nobody is left behind?
2.hint: Count in 8s until you reach or pass 46.
2.why: 5 vans hold 40 children, so 6 children are left. They need one more van. So the school books 6 vans.

2.q: Priya faces east. She turns left, then she turns right round to face the opposite way, then she turns right. Which way does she face now: north, east, south or west?
2.hint: Draw a small compass. Turn one step at a time and write the direction after each turn.
2.why: Facing east, then north, then south, then west. After the turns Priya faces west.

2.q: You multiply an odd number by an even number, such as 3 × 4. Is the answer odd or even?
2.hint: Try 3 × 4, 5 × 2 and 7 × 6. Look at the ones digit of each answer.
2.why: An even number can be split into pairs with none left over. Odd × even means some groups of that even number, so every group still splits into pairs. The answer is even.

2.q: Aisha has 56 stickers and Ben has 38 stickers. Aisha hands some to Ben, and then both children hold equal numbers. How many does Aisha hand over?
2.hint: Find how many more stickers Aisha has. Each sticker she gives moves across the gap.
2.why: Aisha has 18 more than Ben. Giving a sticker makes the gap 2 smaller, so she gives half of 18, which is 9 stickers. Check: they both have 47.

2.q: Siti borrows a book on the 5th and returns it on the 22nd. She has the book on both of those days too. For how many days does she have the book?
2.hint: List each date she has the book, starting on the day she borrows it.
2.why: The dates run from the 5th to the 22nd, both included. 22 − 5 = 17, and the first day needs one more: 18 days.

2.q: Mei Ling sorts these numbers: 12, 25, 30, 45, 18, 50, 36 and 21. She keeps only the numbers that are in the 3 times table and bigger than 20. How many numbers does she keep?
2.hint: Check each number twice: is it in the 3 times table, and is it bigger than 20?
2.why: The numbers that pass both checks are 30, 45, 36, 21. That is 4 numbers.

2.q: A big square is split into 9 small squares, 3 rows of 3. Counting squares of every size, how many squares can you find?
2.hint: Count the 1 by 1 squares, then the 2 by 2 squares, then the whole square.
2.why: 9 small squares, 4 squares that are 2 by 2, and 1 big square. 9 + 4 + 1 = 14 squares.

2.q: A balance is level. The left pan holds weights of 47 g and 28 g. The right pan holds a 40 g weight and one more weight. How many grams does the extra weight weigh?
2.hint: Add up the left pan first. The right pan must weigh the same.
2.why: 47 + 28 = 75. The right pan must also weigh 75 g, so 40 + 35 g = 75.

2.q: A bakery bakes 500 buns. It sells 215 buns before lunch and 140 buns after lunch. How many buns are not sold?
2.hint: Add the buns sold at both times first. Then take that away from 500.

2.q: Aunty has 60 sweets. Ali gets 1/3 of the sweets and Ben gets 1/5 of the sweets. How many more sweets does Ali get than Ben?
2.hint: Find Ali's sweets and Ben's sweets separately.
2.why: Ali gets 20. Ben gets 12. 20 − 12 = 8 sweets.

2.q: Farhan has number cards 12, 25, 38, 47, 63 and 75. How many different pairs of cards add up to 100?
2.hint: Take one card. Which other card makes 100 with it? Check each card in turn.
2.why: The pairs are 25 + 75. Each pair adds up to 100, so there are 1 pairs.

2.q: A library lent 345 books in March and 218 books in April. How many more books did it lend in March than in April?
2.hint: Take the smaller number away from the bigger number.

2.q: A floor has tiles in this pattern again and again: red, blue, blue, white. What colour is the 15th tile?
2.hint: Each pattern has 4 tiles. Write the pattern out in rows of 4.
2.why: The pattern repeats every 4 tiles. Three whole patterns make 12 tiles. Then the 13th is red, the 14th is blue and the 15th is blue.

2.q: Mei Ling has 72 stickers. She sticks 8 stickers on each page of her album. How many pages does she fill?
2.hint: Count in 8s until you reach 72.
2.why: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72. That is 9 counts of 8, so she fills 9 pages.

2.q: In the number 538, how much more is the value of the digit 5 than the value of the digit 3?
2.hint: The 5 is in the hundreds place and the 3 is in the tens place. Write the value of each.
2.why: The 5 means 500. The 3 means 30. 500 − 30 = 470.

2.q: In a number pyramid, each brick is the sum of the two bricks under it. The bottom row has four bricks: 5, 3, 8 and 2. What number is on the top brick?
2.hint: Work up one row at a time. The next row has three bricks.
2.why: The second row is 8, 11 and 10. Keep adding in pairs up to the top brick: 40.

2.q: Farhan lists every number from 1 to 100 that is in the 4 times table. How many numbers are on his list?
2.hint: Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12 ... and see how many 4s fit in 100.
2.why: Four fits into 100 exactly 25 times, so the list runs 4, 8, 12, ... 100. That is 25 numbers.

2.q: At the canteen, Ben buys 2 buns at $1.80 each and a drink for $3.20. How much does he spend altogether?
2.hint: Find the cost of the 2 buns first.

2.q: Siti wants to pay exactly 85 cents. She has many coins of each kind: 5 cents, 10 cents, 20 cents and 50 cents. What is the fewest coins she needs?
2.hint: Start with the biggest coin that is not more than the amount. Then see what is left.
2.why: Use 50 + 20 + 10 + 5. That is 4 coins.

2.q: Ravi stacks balls in triangles. The first stack has 1 ball, the next has 3, the next has 6, the next has 10. Each stack has one more row than the one before. How many balls are in the 7th stack?
2.hint: Look at how many balls each new stack adds: 2, then 3, then 4. What comes next?
2.why: The new balls added are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The stacks hold 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28. The 7th stack has 28 balls.

2.q: One digit in this sum is hidden: 3_8 + 247 = 625. Which digit goes in the blank?
2.hint: Work from the ones column on the right. Carry 1 whenever a column makes ten or more.
2.why: Check 378 + 247 = 625. The hidden digit is 7.

2.q: Mei Ling gave 1/4 of her marbles to her brother and kept 27 marbles. How many marbles did she have at first?
2.hint: If 1/4 was given away, what fraction was kept? How many marbles are in each quarter?
2.why: She kept 3/4, which is 27 marbles. One quarter is 27 ÷ 3 = 9 marbles. The whole is 4 × 9 = 36 marbles.

2.q: A garden has 5 equal sides. Each side is 14 m long. Uncle puts a fence all the way round the garden. How long is the fence?
2.hint: Add the same side length once for each side.

3.q: A bag of rice weighs 3 kg 450 g. How many grams is that?
3.hint: 1 kg is 1000 g. Change the kilograms to grams first.

3.q: 10 children are at a puzzle club. Each pair of children shakes hands exactly once. How many handshakes happen?
3.hint: Each child shakes hands with 10 − 1 others, but each handshake has two children in it.
3.why: Each of the 10 children shakes 9 hands, which makes 90. Each handshake was counted twice, so 90 ÷ 2 = 45 handshakes.

3.q: Hui Min has four digit cards: 2, 5, 7 and 9. She makes two 2-digit numbers using each card once. What is the biggest total she can make by adding the two numbers?
3.hint: The biggest digits should go in the tens places.
3.why: Put 9 and 7 in the tens places and 5 and 2 in the ones places: 72 + 95 = 167.

3.q: A shop has 2 cartons of 1000 staples, 13 boxes of 100 staples, 4 packs of 10 staples and 7 loose staples. How many staples does the shop have?
3.hint: Change each kind of pack into staples. Then add the four amounts.

3.q: A rectangular mat has an area of 96 square centimetres. It is 16 cm long. How wide is the mat?
3.hint: Which number times 16 makes 96?
3.why: 16 × 6 = 96, so the mat is 6 cm wide.

3.q: Class 3A collected 250 cans. Class 3B collected 130 more cans than Class 3A. Class 3C collected 45 fewer cans than Class 3B. How many cans did the three classes collect altogether?
3.hint: Find the cans for Class 3B first. Then Class 3C. Then add all three.

3.q: There are 53 children at a party. Each table seats 6 children. How many tables are needed so that every child has a seat?
3.hint: Count in 6s: 6, 12, 18 ... until you reach or pass 53.
3.why: 8 tables seat 48 children, so 5 children are left. They need one more table. 8 + 1 = 9 tables.

3.q: Find the least 3-digit number in which the three digits add to 15.
3.hint: The hundreds digit should be as small as possible. Then make the tens digit small too.
3.why: Start with the hundreds digit 1. The other two digits must add to 14, so the tens digit should be as small as possible: 5 and 9. The number is 159.

3.q: A stadium holds 3,847 people. What is this number rounded to the nearest hundred? A number exactly halfway rounds up.
3.hint: Look at the tens digit. Is it 5 or more?
3.why: The tens digit is 4, which is less than 5, so the number rounds down to 3800.

3.q: A number pyramid is built so that every brick equals the two bricks beneath it added together. The bottom row reads 3, ?, 4, 2 and the top brick is 32. Which number is hidden in the bottom row?
3.hint: Try a number for the missing brick and work up to the top. Then change it until the top brick is right.
3.why: Working up from the bottom row, the top brick is 32. Try 4: the top is 29. Try 5: the top is 32. So the missing number is 5.

3.q: A cake is cut into 3 equal slices and Ravi eats 2 of them. If the same cake had been cut into 9 equal slices, how many of those slices would Ravi have eaten to eat the same amount?
3.hint: Cut each of the 3 big slices into smaller equal slices. How many small slices does each big slice make?
3.why: Each big slice would be cut into 9 ÷ 3 = 3 small slices. 2 big slices are 2 × 3 = 6 slices.

3.q: A rope is 3 times as long as a string. The rope is 84 cm longer than the string. How long is the rope?
3.hint: Draw a bar for the string and a bar 3 times as long for the rope. How many parts is the difference?
3.why: The string is 1 part and the rope is 3 parts. The difference is 2 parts and it is 84 cm. 1 part = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 cm. The rope is 3 × 42 = 126 cm.

3.q: Ali, Ben, Chen and Dina each play one sport: football, swimming, badminton or tennis. Ali does not play football or tennis. Ben plays swimming. Chen does not play football. Dina does not play badminton. Who plays football?
3.hint: Ben plays swimming, so nobody else does. Then work out who can play each remaining sport.
3.why: Ali plays badminton, Ben plays swimming, Chen plays tennis, Dina plays football. So Dina plays football.

3.q: A strip of flags repeats this pattern again and again: red, red, blue, green. The strip has 30 flags. How many flags are red?
3.hint: How many flags are in one pattern? How many whole patterns fit in 30? What is left over?
3.why: One pattern has 4 flags and 2 are red. 30 = 7 × 4 + 2, so there are 7 whole patterns and 2 flags left over. The 7 patterns have 14 red flags, and the 2 left-over flags are both red. 14 + 2 = 16 flags.

3.q: A window has panes in a grid 3 panes across and 2 panes down. Count every rectangle you can see, including single panes and bigger rectangles made of panes. How many rectangles are there?
3.hint: Count the rectangles by size: 1 by 1, 2 by 1, 1 by 2, and so on. Or choose two vertical lines and two horizontal lines.
3.why: Choose 2 of the 4 vertical lines in 6 ways and 2 of the 3 horizontal lines in 3 ways. 6 × 3 = 18 rectangles.

3.q: The water in a tank is 20 cm deep. It goes up 5, then down 12, then up 9, then down 3. What is the greatest depth the water reaches, in centimetres?
3.hint: Write down the depth after each change. Then find the biggest.
3.why: The depths in order are 20, 25, 13, 22, 19. The greatest depth is 25 cm.

3.q: Mei Ling sorts shells into piles. The first pile has 2 shells, the second has 5, the third has 9, the fourth has 14. Each pile has more shells than the one before, and the extra shells grow by 1 each time. How many shells are in the 8th pile?
3.hint: Look at how many more shells each pile has than the one before: 3, then 4, then 5.
3.why: The extra shells are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. The piles hold 2, 5, 9, 14, 20, 27, 35, 44. The 8th pile has 44 shells.

3.q: In one month, the 5th is a Thursday. What is the date of the 3rd Tuesday in that month?
3.hint: Find the first Tuesday of the month. Then add 7 for each next one.
3.why: The first Tuesday is the 3rd. Adding 7 each time gives the 3rd, 10th and 17th. The 3rd Tuesday is the 17th.

3.q: A meal set has one main, one side and one drink. The stall offers 4 mains, 3 sides and 2 drinks. How many different meal sets can you choose?
3.hint: Pick one main. How many side and drink choices go with it?
3.why: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 meal sets.

3.q: A bag has 1000 beads. 350 beads are red and 275 beads are blue. The rest are green. How many green beads are in the bag?
3.hint: Add the red and blue beads first. Then find how many more make 1000.

3.q: Sam makes a bridge of triangles using straws. One triangle needs 3 straws. Two triangles joined side by side need 5 straws. How many straws do 14 triangles in a row need?
3.hint: Each new triangle shares one side with the one before. How many new straws does it need?
3.why: The first triangle needs 3 straws. Every other triangle adds 2. So 14 triangles need 3 + 13 × 2 = 29 straws.

3.q: Each letter stands for a different digit. AB + CB = BBC. AB and CB are 2-digit numbers and BBC is a 3-digit number. What digit is A?
3.hint: Two numbers with two digits each can never make 200 or more. What does that tell you about B?
3.why: B must be 1. In the ones place 1 + 1 = 2, so C = 2. In the tens place A + 2 must make 11, so A = 9. Check: 91 + 21 = 112.

3.q: In a class of 36 children, 20 are in the swimming club and 17 are in the cycling club. 5 children are in neither club. How many children are in both clubs?
3.hint: Find how many children are in at least one club. Then add the two clubs and compare.
3.why: 31 children are in at least one club. 20 + 17 = 37, and 37 is 6 more than 31. Those 6 were counted twice, so 6 children are in both.

3.q: How many numbers from 50 to 200 are in the 8 times table?
3.hint: Find the first multiple of 8 that is more than 50. Then keep adding 8.
3.why: The multiples of 8 in this range are 56, 64, 72, ... 200. The first is 7 × 8 and the last is 25 × 8, so there are 25 − 7 + 1 = 19 numbers.

3.q: The perimeter of a square tile is 32 cm. Find the area of the tile in square centimetres.
3.hint: A square has 4 equal sides. Find one side first.
3.why: 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so each side is 8 cm. Area: 8 × 8 = 64 cm².

3.q: Mei Ling has 18 square tiles. She puts all of them in equal rows, with the same number of tiles in every row. How many different ways can she do this? (1 row of 18 is one way. 3 rows of 6 and 6 rows of 3 are different ways.)
3.hint: Try 1 row, 2 rows, 3 rows ... and see which numbers of rows work.
3.why: The numbers of rows that work are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18. That is 6 ways.

3.q: In the number 6,482, how much more is the value of the digit 6 than the value of the digit 4?
3.hint: The 6 is in the thousands place and the 4 is in the hundreds place. Write the value of each.

3.q: At the bottom of a 15 m well sits a frog. Each day it climbs 4 m, and each night it slides back 3 m. On which day does it first get out at the top?
3.hint: Find where the frog is at the end of the first day and the first night. Then look for a pattern.
3.why: On day 1 the frog climbs to 4 m. On day 2 it climbs to 5 m, and so on: on day k it climbs to k + 3 m. It first reaches 15 m when k + 3 = 15, so on day 12.

3.q: 5 runners are given lanes 1 to 5 for a race, one runner to each lane. In how many different ways can the lanes be given out?
3.hint: Choose who gets lane 1. Then see how many runners are left for lane 2.
3.why: 5 choices for lane 1, then 4, then 3, then 2, then 1. 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 ways.

3.q: Kumar faces south. He turns right, then left, then left again, then right. Which way does he face now: north, east, south or west?
3.hint: Draw a small compass. Turn one step at a time and write the direction after each turn.
3.why: Facing south, then west, then south, then east, then south. After the turns Kumar faces south.

3.q: A bank gives Mr Tan $115 in $5 notes. How many notes does he get?
3.hint: How many 5s make 115? Count in 5s or use the 5 times table.
3.why: $5, $10, $15 ... Each note is worth $5. $115 ÷ $5 = 23 notes.

4.q: A board is made of small squares, 4 across and 4 down. Counting squares of every size, including the whole board, how many squares can you find?
4.hint: Count the 1 by 1 squares, then the 2 by 2 squares, then the 3 by 3 squares and the 4 by 4 square.

4.q: A table shows the number of visitors to a museum: Monday 1246, Tuesday 1601, Wednesday 1384 and Thursday 1621. How many visitors came on these four days altogether?
4.hint: Add the thousands, then the hundreds, then the tens and ones. Or add two days at a time.

4.q: A floor strip is 6 units long. Tiles that are 1 unit long or 2 units long are laid in a line to cover it exactly. How many different orders of tiles can cover the strip?
4.hint: Find the number of ways for strips of length 1, 2, 3 and 4 first.
4.why: The ways for lengths 1 to 6 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. Each is the sum of the two before it. For length 6 there are 13 ways.

4.q: Wei Jie has five digit cards: 4, 0, 7, 2 and 9. He uses all five cards to make an odd 5-digit number. What is the smallest odd number he can make?
4.hint: An odd number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, and the first digit cannot be 0. Choose the last digit first.
4.why: The last digit must be 7 or 9. Using 7 at the end leaves 0, 2, 4, 9 for the front. The smallest start is 20 then 4 then 9: 20,479.

4.q: A rope is 5 1/2 m long. Kumar cuts off 2 3/4 m. How long is the rope that is left? Give your answer as a mixed number.
4.hint: Change both lengths to quarters before subtracting.

4.q: Priya types 3 × (14 + 6) − 20 into a calculator. What answer should the calculator show?
4.hint: Work out the brackets first. Then multiply. Then subtract.
4.why: Brackets first: 14 + 6 = 20. Then 3 × 20 = 60. Then 60 − 20 = 40.

4.q: Each brick in a number pyramid equals the two bricks under it added together. The bottom row is ?, 4, 6, 3 and the top brick is 50. Which number is hidden?
4.hint: Try a number for the hidden brick and work up to the top. Then adjust it until the top brick is right.
4.why: The hidden brick counts 1 time in the top brick; the next counts 3 times, then 3, then 1. The others add up to 33, and 50 − 33 = 17.

4.q: A 4 by 4 by 4 cube is painted yellow on the outside and cut into 64 small cubes. How many of the small cubes have no yellow paint on them?
4.hint: Take off the outer layer of cubes. What size cube is left in the middle?
4.why: Without the outer layer, a 2 by 2 by 2 cube is left in the middle. 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cubes.

4.q: A diver is 11 m below the surface of a lake. The diver goes deeper by 5, then back up by 8, then deeper by 9, then back up by 3. What is the greatest distance below the surface that the diver reaches? Answer in metres.
4.hint: Write the distance below the surface after each move. Then find the biggest.
4.why: The distances in order are 11, 16, 8, 17, 14. The greatest distance is 17 m.

4.q: How many numbers in the 7 times table are between 100 and 300?
4.hint: Find the first multiple of 7 above 100. Then count on in 7s.
4.why: The first is 105 and the last is 294. From 105 to 294 is 189, and 189 ÷ 7 = 27 steps. 27 steps means 28 numbers. The answer is 28 numbers.

4.q: A school needs 2350 name tags. They are sold in packs of 24. How many packs must the school buy to have enough tags?
4.hint: Divide 2350 by 24. If there is a remainder, what must the school do?
4.why: 2350 ÷ 24 gives 97 packs with 22 tags still needed. 97 packs are not enough, so the school buys 98 packs.

4.q: Hui Min pays exactly 60 cents using 50-cent, 20-cent, 10-cent and 5-cent coins. She may leave out a kind of coin if she likes. How many different sets of coins can she use?
4.hint: Count by the 50-cent coins: she uses none or one. Then count the ways to make the rest.
4.why: With no 50-cent coin, 60 cents is made from 20-, 10- and 5-cent coins in 16 ways... With one 50-cent coin, 10 cents are left: 2 ways. Altogether 18 sets.

4.q: Priya is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Mei Ling. Mei Ling is taller than Ravi. Ravi is taller than Sam. Who is in the middle?
4.hint: Write the five names in a row from shortest to tallest.
4.why: From shortest to tallest: Sam, Ravi, Mei Ling, Ben, Priya. The one in the middle is Mei Ling.

4.q: Farhan builds towers of cubes. The first tower has 3 cubes, the second has 5, the third has 8 and the fourth has 12. Each tower has more cubes than the one before, and the extra cubes grow by 1 each time. How many cubes are in the 9th tower?
4.hint: Look at how many more cubes each tower has than the one before: 2, then 3, then 4.
4.why: The extra cubes are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. The towers hold 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, 38, 47. The 9th tower has 47 cubes.

4.q: Mei Ling is dressing up for the school show. She has 3 tops, 4 skirts and 5 hats, and she wears one of each. How many costumes are possible?
4.hint: Pick a top. How many skirt and hat choices go with it?
4.why: 3 × 4 × 5 = 60 outfits.

4.q: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be 365 days from today?
4.hint: There are 7 days in a week. How many days are left over after whole weeks?
4.why: 365 = 52 × 7 + 1, so after 52 whole weeks it is Wednesday again, and one more day makes Thursday.

4.q: Arjun works out (20 + 16) ÷ 9 × 5. Work from left to right, doing the brackets first. What is his answer?
4.hint: Do the bracket first. Then divide. Then multiply.
4.why: Bracket: 20 + 16 = 36. Divide: 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Multiply: 4 × 5 = 20.

4.q: Figure 1 uses 5 tiles, Figure 2 uses 9 tiles and Figure 3 uses 13 tiles. The figures keep growing in the same way. How many tiles does Figure 15 use?
4.hint: How many tiles does each figure add? Use it to build a rule from the figure number.
4.why: Each figure adds 4 tiles. The rule is 4 × figure number + 1. For Figure 15: 4 × 15 + 1 = 61 tiles.

4.q: Farhan has $85 and Hui Min has $47. Farhan gives Hui Min some money, and then they have the same amount. How many dollars does Farhan give?
4.hint: Find how many more dollars Farhan has. Each dollar he gives moves across the gap.
4.why: Farhan has $38 more. Each dollar given makes the gap 2 smaller, so he gives half of 38, which is 19 dollars. Check: they both have $66.

4.q: A warehouse has 12 cartons of 1000 pencils, 18 boxes of 100 pencils, 7 packs of 10 pencils and 5 loose pencils. How many pencils are in the warehouse?
4.hint: Change each kind of pack into pencils. Then add the four amounts.

4.q: In a chess club, 12 players each play one game against every other player. How many games are played?
4.hint: Each player plays 12 − 1 games, but each game has two players.
4.why: Each of the 12 players plays 11 games, which makes 132. Each game was counted twice, so 132 ÷ 2 = 66 games.

4.q: A night train leaves at 21:50 and arrives at 02:15 the next day. How many minutes does the journey take?
4.hint: Count the time from 21:50 to midnight. Then add the time from midnight to 02:15.
4.why: From 21:50 to midnight is 130 minutes. From midnight to 02:15 is 135 minutes. 130 + 135 = 265 minutes.

4.q: Two shops sold 1250 mooncakes in all. Shop A sold 340 more mooncakes than Shop B. How many mooncakes did Shop A sell?
4.hint: Take away the extra 340. Share what is left equally between the two shops.
4.why: 1250 − 340 = 910. 910 ÷ 2 = 455 for Shop B. Shop A sold 455 + 340 = 795 mooncakes.

4.q: How many vertices (corners) do a cube and a triangular prism have altogether? A triangular prism has two triangle ends and three rectangle sides.
4.hint: Count the vertices of each solid separately. Then add.
4.why: Counting separately, a cube has 8 vertices and a triangular prism has 6 vertices. Altogether that is 14 vertices.

4.q: 5 notebooks cost $12.50. A shop sells every notebook at the same price. How much do 6 notebooks cost?
4.hint: Find the cost of 1 notebook first.
4.why: 1 notebook costs $2.50. 6 notebooks cost 6 × $2.50 = $15.

4.q: A rectangular noticeboard has a border of 60 cm all the way round its edge. The board is 17 cm long. How wide is the board?
4.hint: The two long sides use 17 + 17. What is left for the two short sides?

4.q: Farhan runs 9.6 km in 4 equal laps. How long is one lap in kilometres?
4.hint: Share 9.6 into 4 equal parts. 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 1.6 ÷ 4 = 0.4.

4.q: A park path is 3 km 250 m long. How many metres is that?
4.hint: 1 km is 1000 m. Change the kilometres to metres first.

4.q: A palindrome is a number that stays the same when its digits are written in reverse order, like 1331. How many 4-digit palindromes are there?
4.hint: The last digit must match the first digit, and the two middle digits must match each other. Count the choices for the first digit and the second digit.
4.why: The first digit can be 1 to 9, and the second digit can be 0 to 9. The last two digits are then fixed. 9 × 10 = 90 numbers.

4.q: Aisha, Ben, Chen and Dina each have a different hobby: painting, chess, swimming or violin. Aisha does not paint or play chess. Ben swims. Chen does not play the violin. Dina does not swim or paint. Who plays chess?
4.hint: Ben swims, so nobody else does. Then see what is left for each person.
4.why: Aisha has the hobby of violin, Ben has the hobby of swimming, Chen has the hobby of painting, Dina has the hobby of chess. So Dina plays chess.

4.q: A robot faces west. It turns right, then turns right again, then turns to face the opposite way, then turns left. Which way does it face now: north, east, south or west?
4.hint: Draw a small compass. Turn one step at a time and write the direction after each turn.
4.why: Facing west, then north, then east, then west, then south. After the turns the robot faces south.
